criteria.title: Separate public interfaces from implementation and platform detail. - capstone composition
criteria.task: Design register adapter, acquisition driver, scheduler and portable framing interfaces for the F439 teaching firmware. Compare a superloop and an interrupt-to-foreground queue. Enumerate execution contexts, permitted reentrancy and ownership for each buffer. Keep register addresses, IRQ control and Linux descriptors out of the portable interface. Compare plain status/out-parameters with the registered errors.result fixed tagged-value contract. Select one representation and state exactly what C diagnostics, runtime tags and discipline enforce; inspect strict-target header/object dependencies before any actual import.
criteria.purpose: A RAM mock and a board adapter have identical semantics because their C signatures match.

security.scope: Original local teaching service/firmware models and synthetic data only. Physical work is a separately authorized dedicated-board task, not performed by authoring.
security.target: Original telemetry service, scripted adapter or firmware state model named in this exact criterion.
security.environment: C17 local process/model with bounded input and storage; native kernel work only in a disposable VM and physical work only on a dedicated teaching target when separately authorized.
security.attacker_capabilities: Chooses synthetic frame bytes, request timing, allowed completion order and explicitly injected model faults. Does not control trusted authorization or host security policy.
security.isolation: No external target, deployed equipment, credentials or real data; use private temporary files and process-local pipes/socket pairs. Never disable host mitigations or execute an invalid native control transfer.
security.defect: A checksum and a watchdog together establish a safe authorized command path.
security.exposing_transition: Model unauthorized command bytes, valid high-rate telemetry, stalled acquisition and reset as separate threats/faults. Define safe outputs and a trusted authorization boundary outside CRC framing. Use synthetic accepted-message and actuator-state integers only; compare boot, RUNNING, RECOVERING and SAFE_STOP states.
security.exploitability_limits: Only the stated synthetic effect, lifetime/resource violation or model selection error is claimed. A crash/diagnostic is not arbitrary code execution; physical/security enforcement is not inferred from a host model.
security.success_condition: Malformed or unauthorized requests never change protected synthetic state; overload has bounded rejection and recovery cannot repeatedly reapply a partially completed command. Hardware output state remains a separate required observation.
security.repair: Restore the exact admission, ownership, progress, isolation or validity invariant specified in the task; compare the original local defective control with the corrected implementation.
security.regression: Check Malformed or unauthorized requests never change protected synthetic state; overload has bounded rejection and recovery cannot repeatedly reapply a partially completed command. Hardware output state remains a separate required observation. Also retain an ordinary valid successful workflow and a deliberately faulty control that fails for the intended semantic reason.
security.residual_limits: Same-process memory discipline, actual adapter behavior, physical hardware, tool/model assumptions and unsupported threat capabilities remain separately bounded.
